docs.title: QUANTAURA-Core
docs.text:
Agent Execution Authorization Kernel — runtime control plane for AI agents.

No execution occurs without a verified, authorized intent.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Quickstart — run the API in under a minute
  2. Kernel — state machine, policy, crypto
  3. Integrations — LangChain / LangGraph
  4. Commercial — packaging & design partners
  5. API — HTTP surface including audit export

Research modules (simulation, quant, cognitive) live under quantaura/core/ for teams building agentic research systems on top of the same authorization loop.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Agent / Tool Call
       |
       v
 Python SDK  -->  signs payload
       |
       v
 Intent API
  - hash + verify signature
  - policy evaluation
  - multi-party approvals
  - state machine
  - durable SQLite ledger + audit log
       |
  AUTHORIZED --> execute --> COMMITTED
  PENDING --> human gate
  REJECTED

docs.title: LangChain / LangGraph
docs.text:
pip install 'quantaura-core[langchain]'

from quantaura.crypto.signatures import generate_keypair
from quantaura.sdk.python.client import IntentClient
from quantaura.integrations.langchain_tools import protect_langchain_tool

priv, _ = generate_keypair()
client = IntentClient("http://localhost:8000", "lc-agent", priv)

def write_row(msg: str) -> str:
    return f"wrote:{msg}"

gated = protect_langchain_tool(write_row, client=client, action_type="DATABASE_WRITE")
gated(msg="hello")

Every invocation submits a signed intent; the underlying function runs only if status is AUTHORIZED.

docs.title: REST
docs.text: Any language can POST /v1/intents with X-Tenant-ID and optional X-QUANTAURA-Signature. See API.

docs.title: Invariant
docs.text: No execution occurs without a verified, authorized intent.

docs.title: Intent lifecycle
docs.text:
DRAFT
  |
  +-> PENDING_AUTHORIZATION --> AUTHORIZED --> COMMITTED --> COMPENSATED
  |         |                       |
  |         +-----------------------+--> REJECTED
  |
  +-> REJECTED

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
• Canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace)
  • SHA-256 hash
  • Ed25519 signatures (PyNaCl)

docs.title: Multi-party approvals
docs.text: POST /v1/intents/{id}/approve with header X-Actor. Requires N distinct approvers when required_approvals > 1.
